name: EmbeddingGemma 2
intro:
Audio–text retrieval, modality signatures,
and the limits of an alignment experiment.
version: Repository experiment · protocol and interpretation limits in the full report

chapters.title:
Can a voice
find its words?
chapters.subtitle: Paired dialogue, across modalities.
paragraphs: Exp 1 studies 221 paired dialogues from six children. It asks whether a text embedding can retrieve its paired audio embedding, and whether an audio embedding can retrieve its paired text.
This is a retrieval experiment in the original embedding space. Projection plots are exploratory views, not the space in which retrieval metrics were computed.
chapters.note: Exp 1 only. Three pairs were checked directly; the remaining 218 were assumed aligned.

chapters.title:
Read both
directions.
chapters.subtitle: The query modality changes the task.
paragraphs: Text-to-audio Top-1 is 72.4%, while audio-to-text Top-1 is 65.6%. Top-5 and MRR describe additional aspects of the same retrieval evaluation.
A directional difference is not an error in the chart. Each direction chooses queries from a different modality and ranks the opposite candidate set.
chapters.note: These are reported Exp 1 metrics, not a live model running in this page.

chapters.title:
Retrieval can work.
Separation can remain.
chapters.subtitle: A shared task does not erase modality.
paragraphs: The reported mean cosine similarity is about 0.810 for paired examples and 0.720 for mismatched examples. The average gap is about 0.090.
At the same time, held-out-child modality classification reached 100%, and the cosine modality silhouette was approximately 0.226. Retrieval and modality separation coexist.
chapters.note: The gap summarizes this dataset. UMAP is exploratory; it does not prove semantic equivalence.

chapters.title:
Look below
the average.
chapters.subtitle: Six children, unequal sample counts.
paragraphs: The overall result aggregates children with different numbers of paired dialogues. Child-level retrieval reveals variation that a single headline can hide.
Small groups can produce unstable rates. A child with 12 pairs and 100% Top-1 is not evidence of a universal performance guarantee.
chapters.note: These per-child rates describe Exp 1 only. Group size and the alignment assumptions matter.

chapters.title:
Keep the result.
Keep the uncertainty.
chapters.subtitle: What this experiment actually supports.
paragraphs: Cross-modal retrieval works in this setup, while a strong modality signature persists. That is a narrower conclusion than claiming complete semantic alignment.
Only three alignments were reviewed directly, and independent gold topic labels were unavailable. Read the full protocol and results before extending the conclusion.
chapters.note: The original notes, result distributions, and projection figures remain available in the report.
